1.title: Securing Access to Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Securing Access to Storage. It covers the exam area Implement and manage storage. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Configure Azure Storage firewalls and virtual networks. Create and use shared access signature (S A S) tokens. Configure stored access policies. Manage access keys. Configure identity-based access for Azure Files. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement and manage storage (fifteen-twenty percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft Learn A Z-one hundred four study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-six, two thousand twenty-three.

1.title: Firewalls and virtual networks
1.text: Firewalls and virtual networks. By default a storage account accepts requests from all networks. You can restrict access. Selected networks. Allow only chosen virtual networks (subnets) and I P address ranges; everything else is denied. Service endpoint. Lets a subnet reach storage over the Azure backbone; add the subnet to the storage firewall. Private endpoint. Gives the account a private I P address in your V net (through Private Link). Trusted Azure services exception. Allows certain Azure services (such as Backup) through the firewall. Disabled. No public network access; use private endpoints only.

1.title: Firewalls and virtual networks, continued
1.text: Firewalls and virtual networks. The figure shows this: A storage firewall allowing a subnet and an I P range, and a private endpoint. Exam tip: "Only V Ms in one subnet may access the storage account" equals storage firewall with a virtual network rule (service endpoint) or a private endpoint.

1.title: Shared access signatures (SAS)
1.text: Shared access signatures (S A S). A S A S token is a signed U R L query string that gives limited, time-bound access to storage without sharing the account key. User delegation S A S. Signed with: Microsoft Entra credentials. Notes: Most secure; Blob and Data Lake only. Service S A S. Signed with: The account key. Notes: One service (blob, file, queue, table). Account S A S. Signed with: The account key. Notes: One or more services. A S A S defines permissions (read, write, delete, list), start and expiry time, optional allowed I P addresses, and H T T P S-only. Exam tip: A S A S signed with the account key stops working only when it expires, or when you rotate the key or delete the stored access policy it uses.

1.title: Stored access policies
1.text: Stored access policies. A stored access policy is defined on a container, share, queue or table and holds the S A S settings (permissions, start, expiry). A service S A S can reference the policy. Revoke or change. Edit or delete the policy to change or revoke all S A S tokens that use it, without regenerating account keys. Limit. Up to five policies per container, share, queue or table.

1.title: Access keys
1.text: Access keys. Each account has two access keys. A key gives full access to the whole account (shared key authorization), so protect it. Two keys. Rotate one while apps use the other. Store keys in Azure Key Vault. Never in code. Prefer Entra I D and R B A C, or S A S. Keys are all-powerful. Disallow shared key access. Forces Entra I D authorization.

1.title: Identity-based access for Azure Files
1.text: Identity-based access for Azure Files. Azure Files shares (S M B) can authenticate users with identities instead of the account key. On-premises Active Directory Domain Services. Domain-joined clients. Microsoft Entra Domain Services. Cloud-only or hybrid, managed domain. Microsoft Entra Kerberos. Hybrid identities, without domain controllers in Azure.

1.title: Identity-based access for Azure Files, continued
1.text: Identity-based access for Azure Files. Access combines share-level permissions (Azure R B A C roles such as Storage File Data S M B (Server Message Block) Share Contributor) and N T F S file-level permissions. Blob data also supports Entra I D authorization with roles such as Storage Blob Data Contributor. Exam tip: "Users should sign in to the file share with their own domain identity" equals identity-based access for Azure Files plus R B A C roles on the share.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A storage account must be reachable only from one subnet. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A storage firewall virtual network rule with a service endpoint. Network rules restrict access to chosen subnets.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A partner needs read access to one container for twenty-four hours without receiving the account key. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A S A S token with read permission and a twenty-four-hour expiry. A S A S gives limited, time-bound access.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An issued S A S must be revocable without rotating account keys. What should have been used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A stored access policy. Deleting or editing the stored access policy revokes the S A S tokens that reference it.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which S A S type is signed with Microsoft Entra credentials and is the most secure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: User delegation S A S. User delegation S A S avoids using the account key.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Why do accounts have two access keys? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: So one can be rotated while applications use the other. Two keys allow rotation without downtime.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Domain users must access an Azure Files share with their own identities. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Identity-based authentication with R B A C roles on the share. Identity-based access plus share-level roles uses user identities.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a S A S token provide? Answer: Limited, time-bound access without sharing the account key. Question two. What is a stored access policy for? Answer: Managing and revoking S A S tokens without regenerating keys. Question three. How many access keys does an account have? Answer: Two.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which S A S type uses Entra credentials? Answer: User delegation S A S. Question five. What does a private endpoint give a storage account? Answer: A private I P address in your virtual network. Question six. Name one identity source for Azure Files. Answer: For example on-premises A D D S, Microsoft Entra Domain Services or Entra Kerberos.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Network: firewall rules, service endpoint, private endpoint, trusted services. S A S: user delegation (Entra), service, account; permissions, expiry, I P, H T T P S. Stored access policy: revoke or change service S A S without new keys; five per resource. Keys: two keys, rotate, Key Vault, prefer Entra I D and R B A C. Azure Files identity: A D D S, Entra Domain Services, Entra Kerberos plus R B A C and N T F S.
